claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's great to know about Alex.

Now, could you please tell me if you are currently living in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

Next, could you tell me about your living situation with Alex? Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Lovely, thank you for confirming that.

Just a couple more questions to make sure everything is in order:

Is Alex currently in any of the following situations?
- In hospital
- In local authority care
- In residential accommodation

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, actually Alex has been in hospital for a while now - it's been a few months.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital. I hope they're doing okay.

Since Alex has been in hospital for a few months, I need to ask a bit more about this situation. Could you tell me roughly how long Alex has been in hospital? Specifically, has it been more than 12 weeks?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been more than 12 weeks - about 15 weeks now actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, there are some additional factors that could affect your eligibility.

You may still be able to receive Child Benefit if you regularly spend money on Alex while they're in hospital. This could include things like gifts, treats, clothes, or other items for them.

Do you regularly spend money on Alex while they are in hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, unfortunately I haven't been able to afford to spend money on their needs while they're in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for being honest about your situation. I understand that can be difficult.

Just to confirm one last thing: Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for answering all my questions. Based on the information you've provided, I've assessed your eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Outcome for Alex: Not currently eligible**

Here's why:

Under normal circumstances, you would qualify for Child Benefit for Alex since you live in the UK and Alex normally lives with you. However, when a child has been in hospital for more than 12 weeks, Child Benefit eligibility is affected.

Since Alex has been in hospital for approximately 15 weeks (exceeding the 12-week threshold), you would usually no longer be entitled to Child Benefit unless you regularly spend money on them while they're in hospital. As you've mentioned you haven't been able to afford to do this, unfortunately you don't currently meet the exception criteria.

**What you can do:**
- If your circumstances change and you are able to start regularly spending money on Alex while they're in hospital, you may become eligible again.
- When Alex is discharged from hospital and returns home, you should be able to claim Child Benefit again.
- If you'd like to discuss your specific situation further or have any questions, I'd recommend contacting the Child Benefit Office directly, as they can provide guidance tailored to your circumstances.

I'm sorry I couldn't give you better news. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
